title: Connectedness Thresholds for Pseudospectra of Tridiagonal Toeplitz Matrices
content: We study the open Euclidean-norm pseudospectra of \(A_n(a)=\operatorname{tridiag}(a,0,1)\), where \(0<a<1\). For each order \(n\), connectedness is equivalent to \(\varepsilon>\gamma_n(a)\), where \(\gamma_n(a)\) is the maximum of \(s_{\min}(xI_n-A_n(a))\) over the real spectral interval. Every pseudospectral component is contractible. The thresholds decrease strictly with \(n\), so connectedness, once attained, persists at every larger order. The proof uses vertical monotonicity of the least singular value, a symmetric matrix pencil, and separate comparisons for noncentral and central spectral gaps. Explicit upper and lower bounds show that \(\gamma_n(a)\asymp_a{(n+1)a^{n/2}}\). Consequently, the first connected order equals \(2[\log(1/\varepsilon)+\log\log(1/\varepsilon)]/\log(1/a)+O_a(1)\) as \(\varepsilon\) tends to zero. We also give the connectedness thresholds at \(a=0\) and \(a=1\).
